deliverable_4_scaffold: No new code — deliverable 4 is 'Benchmark delta vs. base model (+3pp LiveCodeBench)'. The eval harness from deliverable 3 IS the measurement tool. The baseline (P) is `npm run eval:baseline` against the bare trained-model; the trained number is `npm run eval:trained` against trained-model; delta = trained - baseline. The no-DPO baseline (Q) is scaffolded via the CLI's --no-dpo option stub (not exercised; awaits the first Modal run)

architecture_decisions.D1_azr_join_key: A (tag-based). The join surface is (task_type, content_hash). Deterministic, idempotent, no embedding-similarity dependency. The schema also stores problem_hash (sha256 of normalized problem text) for the future embedding-similarity path; we don't query on it yet but it's free to add later.
architecture_decisions.D2_weight_reload_mechanism: Y (HTTP/Ollama adapter reload). Decision documented in src/coordinator/lora-reloader.js's docblock. The coordinator's model router already calls Ollama; we just needed to keep Ollama's loaded-model list in sync with the trainer's symlink swap. The X (in-process transformers) and Z (lazy background reload) alternatives were considered and rejected because X adds a Python dependency to the coordinator (breaking the Node-only service) and Z has a 1-cycle staleness window that defeats the point of the trainer's atomic symlink swap.
architecture_decisions.D3_eval_baseline: R (both baselines, P first). P is free and immediate: `npm run eval:baseline` runs against qwen2.5:7b. Q is scaffolded in the CLI driver (--no-dpo flag) but not exercised — no Modal run is available yet. The first real Modal run will produce a Q checkpoint; the operator runs the same harness against both P and Q checkpoints, subtracts, and reports the delta.
architecture_decisions.outcome_filter_lenient_policy: The azr_result rule implements the LENIENT reading of ADR-020 Decision 2 ('AZR pass/fail gates <meta-rl-pipeline>'): records with a verified AZR pass are kept (positive signal); records with a verified AZR fail are excluded by construction (the trainer's query only populates the index with passed=true); records with NO AZR result are also kept (missing data, not a verified negative). Rationale: the strict reading ('drop unverified') would yield empty datasets for the first few training cycles because the index is small relative to the corpus, which defeats the iterative improvement loop. The lenient policy matches min_score_gap's missing-scores policy and lets the corpus grow naturally.
architecture_decisions.verdict_shape_change: Changed the outcome-filter's _applyRule return from a bare string ('keep' or reason) to a structured {action, reason} object. This was needed to support the azr_result rule's unverified-but-kept case (where we want to keep the record but optionally surface a marker in the debug log). The verdict shape change is internal — the public FilterResult ({kept, dropped, stats}) shape is unchanged. Existing tests for min_score_gap and tag_match still pass because they assert on result.dropped[i].reason (the reason string, which is the same string we put in the new verdict's reason field).
architecture_decisions.eval_harness_ollama_choice: Used Ollama (not transformers.js) for eval inference. Rationale: Ollama is already the AWARE 2.0 inference sidecar (ADR-020 Decision 3); reusing it means no new dependency, no extra GPU memory pressure, and the same code path the real /coordinate call uses (so eval results are representative). The baseline (no LoRA) is just 'POST to Ollama with a different model name' — no special path needed.
architecture_decisions.eval_harness_in_repo_fixtures: 5 GSM8K + 5 LiveCodeBench problems in-repo. Rationale: pulls of the full benchmarks would dominate test runtime and add a network dependency at test time. The 5+5 are enough to smoke-test the harness plumbing and to surface a meaningful accuracy number for the first trained run. Operators who want the full benchmark drop their own problem set into ./eval-fixtures/ and pass --fixtures=<dir>.
architecture_decisions.lora_reloader_failure_restore: The poll-driven _tick() restores lastTarget to the previous value when _doReload returns {ok: false} or throws. Rationale: if we didn't restore, the next poll would see (prev=current, current=new) and the shouldReload() comparison would return false (we already 'moved' to the new target) — we'd silently miss the swap. By restoring, we ensure the next poll detects the same pending change and retries. This is the standard 'optimistic update with rollback on failure' pattern.

operator_runbook_for_deliverable_5.step_3_wait_for_first_run: psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 18432 -U aware -d aware2 -c "SELECT run_id, status, n_pairs, started_at, completed_at FROM aware_training_runs ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 1;"

follow_ups: Deliv 5 (real benchmark delta) — hard-blocked on the operator's first Modal training run. Documented the 7-step runbook above. After the first real run, the operator can re-run npm run eval:baseline + npm run eval:trained and report the delta.

Outcome-filter 'azr_result' lenient policy — if a future use case wants strict gating (drop unverified), implement a separate 'require_azr' rule rather than changing the existing rule's behavior (which would break the filter-level contract for any operator relying on the current behavior).
Eval harness — full LiveCodeBench + GSM8K benchmark pull (hundreds of problems) is out of scope for this slice. Operators who want the full numbers drop a custom fixtures dir with --fixtures=<path>.

Bring-up 8m smoke — uses `node --input-type=module` to avoid the async-import race. If Node ever drops the --input-type flag, this smoke needs to migrate to a .mjs file in the repo. (The .mjs file is itself a tiny change but is a dependency to track.)
